name: GIMP batch
role: Headless GIMP via --batch and a selected interpreter; heavyweight, version-specific procedures
summary: GIMP's non-interactive mode uses --batch and --batch-interpreter, then --quit. GIMP 3's python-fu-eval interpreter exposes the Gimp and Gio APIs, while the procedure database provides format-specific import and export operations. Procedure signatures differ between GIMP 2 and 3, so scripts are version-specific. Distinguishing strength: reproducing GIMP-only operations without the GUI.
use_when: A GIMP-specific operation (layer modes, plug-in filter, XCF layers) has no CLI equivalent elsewhere
Batch-converting or editing existing .xcf files with layers intact
Reusing an existing batch routine unchanged after confirming its GIMP major version
avoid_when: Resize, crop, convert, annotate: ImageMagick starts faster and is the validated baseline
Colour-managed or EXR sequence work: oiiotool
Needing stability across GIMP majors: scripts break between 2.10 and 3
notes: 2026-11-16: GIMP 3.2.8 on macOS ran python-fu-eval with --no-interface and loaded Gimp.file_load plus the file-png-export PDB procedure. The example validates one PPM-to-PNG roundtrip; startup also logged attempts to write the user's GIMP config directory, which the sandbox denied.
2026-11-16: GIMP 3 Python batch execution is confirmed on this host. Python-Fu and PDB procedure signatures remain version-specific; no cross-platform or GIMP 2 claim is made.

assessment.rationale: GIMP 3.2.6 released 2026-09-10 per gimp.org downloads; man page documents the GIMP 3 batch interface. Valid but heavyweight and version-bound; a niche behind ImageMagick for scripted edits.

evidence.result: Loaded an owned 16x12 PPM through Gimp.file_load, exported it through the file-png-export PDB procedure, and verified three exact pixel samples in the PNG.
evidence.scope: GIMP 3.2.8 Python batch on macOS arm64 for PPM import and PNG export; does not cover XCF editing, other PDB procedures, or other platforms.
